origin.note: Walk 19's tags were the first per-document data people typed; comments with mentions are the cross-cutting version: schema, API, notifications and preferences, escaping, docs.

title: Comments on documents, with @mentions
objective: Let library members discuss a document. Store comments in their own table through a new migration. `POST /api/documents/:id/comments` with `{ body }` adds one (201 `{ comment: { id, docId, authorId, body, createdAt } }`; the body is trimmed and must be 1 to 2000 characters, else 400 `invalid_body`); `GET /api/documents/:id/comments` lists them oldest first. Only members of the document's library may do either. A comment can mention people by email, as `@tom@northwind.example`: each mentioned member of the library gets one email (a new notification type `comment.mention`, turned off by a new preference `mentions`, naming the author and the document); people outside the library and the author themself get nothing. The document page lists the comments with `data-testid` `comment`, `comment-author` (the author's name) and `comment-body`. Keep docs/notifications.md current. Add tests.
acceptance: A new migration creates the comments table; migrations 1 to 3 are unchanged; an upgraded database takes comments
Members add and list comments oldest first, with validation (400 invalid_body) and 404 for outsiders
@mentions email each mentioned library member once, never outsiders or the author, and respect the mentions preference
The document page lists comments with author names, escaped
docs/notifications.md lists comment.mention and its preference
plan_summary: Migration 004 and a comments repository; a comments service with mention parsing through the notifier; a new notification type and preference; routes; the document view lists comments; docs/notifications.md; tests.
